root_cause_label: Hallucinated Walkthrough and Maze Navigation Failure
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent applied a fabricated internal Zork I walkthrough that was geographically incorrect, and after its failure was unable to navigate the maze or retrieve a valid walkthrough due to bot detection on search engines.
t_err_evidence: In step 10, the agent writes a long command sequence as a single-line heredoc using literal '\n' characters (proxy shortcut attempt), acting on an unverified internal belief about the correct Zork I command sequence. The walkthrough references items and locations (e.g., 'take trident', 'take painting', 'take torch') that are not in the starting area, indicating the agent fabricated a walkthrough rather than grounding it in the game state.
t_commit_evidence: In step 34, the agent enters the Maze of twisty little passages for the first time. From this point, every direction attempted either loops back to an identical maze room or hits dead ends. The agent has no items to use as markers (having left them behind or not yet collected many), no valid walkthrough, and no systematic mapping strategy. Given the agent's actual behavior pattern of random direction guessing, the failing outcome is locked in.
t_surface_evidence: In step 12, after executing the corrected walkthrough script (step 11), every action returns 'You can't see any X here!' or navigates to wrong rooms. The game score stays at 0, confirming the walkthrough was geographically invalid for the actual game state. The agent's own analysis notes 'the walkthrough is wrong for this Zork version.'
trigger_explanation: The agent acted on the unverified premise that it possessed an accurate internal Zork I command sequence. The walkthrough assumed a specific room layout and item locations that differ from the actual game (e.g., attempting to 'take lamp' and 'take rug' while in the Forest outside the house, trying 'take Trident' in a dimly lit forest). This false premise caused the agent to waste many moves and misalign its subsequent strategy.
forewarning_evidence: In step 10, the initial cat heredoc attempt fails immediately with 'cat: mailboxnread: No such file or directory' because literal '\n' characters were used instead of newlines. This was an immediate signal that the command construction was flawed. The agent noticed and rewrote the script in step 11, but did not question whether the walkthrough content itself was correct.
fabrication_evidence: In steps 10-11, the agent writes a long sequence of game commands referencing items and rooms (trident, coffin, painting, torch, case, skull, sceptre, necklace, bracelet, map, shovel, slide, brochure) that either don't exist in Zork I or are not accessible from the starting location. The agent treats this internally-generated sequence as a valid walkthrough, which is a fabricated proxy solution rather than actual game knowledge.
